title: Best AI Agent Builders in 2026 (Ranked and Compared)
summary: The 2026 free AI agent builder matrix no other guide publishes: verified free-tier limits, plan vs trial, real actions, and public publishing, tool by tool.

Best Free AI Agent Builders…


On this page (23)


The best free AI agent builders in 2026 let you build and run an AI agent that plans multi-step work, uses real tools, and acts on your data, at zero cost, with no credit card required. That promise is not uniform. Some platforms stay free indefinitely; others only look free until a countdown ends. This guide verifies 20 AI agent builders' free tiers tool by tool, checking four things most ranking pages skip: is free a permanent plan or a time-boxed trial, can a free agent run a real integration action, can a free agent publish publicly, and what usage or knowledge limit caps it hardest.


> **TL;DR:** Of 20 AI agent builders checked in September 2026, 11 stay free indefinitely, including Taskade, Zapier Agents, Make, Relevance AI and self-hosted n8n. Lindy and Gumloop are now time-boxed trials. Taskade is the strongest no-code pick for publishing a public agent on Free (1 agent, 1 knowledge item).[Build an agent free →](https://www.taskade.com/agents)


Choosing well matters more than it used to.[Gartner predicts that over 40% of agentic AI projects will be canceled by the end of 2027](https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2025-06-25-gartner-predicts-over-40-percent-of-agentic-ai-projects-will-be-canceled-by-end-of-2027) , citing escalating costs, unclear value, and weak controls. Starting free and outgrowing the free tier on purpose, rather than hitting an unadvertised wall, is the cheapest way to de-risk that bet. If you want the concepts before the comparison, our[AI agent builders explained](https://www.taskade.com/blog/agent-builders-explained) primer covers how they work and how to choose.

## Plan or Trial? The Free Tiers That Aren't Actually Free in 2026


Most builders that advertise "free" in 2026 fall into one of two groups, and the difference decides whether you can evaluate a tool on your own schedule or against someone else's clock. A forever-free plan renews its allowance every month (or every day) for as long as you keep the account. A time-boxed trial gives you the full paid product for a fixed number of days, then asks for a card or locks you out.

Google Opal is the extreme case worth calling out by name: it is a Google Labs experiment with no paid tier announced as of September 2026, so there is currently no wall to hit at all, though Google has not said whether that changes once the product leaves Labs. At the other end, Copilot Studio never had a standalone free plan to remove — it has always billed in Copilot Credits or run on an existing Microsoft 365 Copilot seat.


The question that actually predicts your experience is not "does it say free," it is where the free path leads:


## What a Free AI Agent Can Actually Do


An agent that can only chat is not the same product as an agent that can send an email, update a record, or publish where a customer can reach it — and "free tier" alone does not tell you which one you are getting. Three limits decide it, and each vendor caps a different one hardest.


What gets capped hardest The typical wall Who caps it this way


**Knowledge the agent can hold** 1 to 50 sources or items Taskade (1 item/agent on Free), Voiceflow (50 sources)


**Real integration actions** Paid-only, or metered as "activities" Botpress (paid only), Zapier Agents (400 activities/mo, counts triggers + actions + lookups)


**Public publishing itself** Excluded from free, or a separate product Botpress (excluded), Zapier Agents (needs Chatbots, a different product)


**Concurrent or daily runs** 1 task or a daily credit reset Manus (1 concurrent task, 300 credits/day), n8n Cloud (trial only)


**Agents or crews per account** 1 to 3 Taskade (1 agent), Gumloop and Stack AI-style tools (project caps), MindStudio (1 agent), CrewAI Studio (1 crew)


A knowledge-item cap ends quietly: the agent keeps answering, just from less context than you expected. A publishing cap ends loudly: you build something you cannot show anyone without upgrading. If you have to accept one, the knowledge cap is cheaper to work around — the publishing cap is not.

## What Is the Best Free AI Agent Builder in 2026?


Taskade is the strongest free-tier pick for a no-code team that wants a group of agents working inside a shared workspace, because publishing a Free-plan agent to a public link works today, with no upgrade required — the tradeoff is a hard 1-agent, 1-knowledge-item ceiling until you move to a paid plan starting at $10 per month billed annually. That said, "best" still depends on the job. Zapier Agents and Make give the most real automation actions on a plan that never expires. Google Opal is the only tool here with no paid tier at all. n8n and CrewAI win for self-hosting and developers who want full control in code.


The builders below fall into four groups. The map shows where each one sits — Relay.app's old slot now goes to Make, a live, forever-free alternative for the same no-code, workflow-first use case.

## How We Ranked These AI Agent Builders


We ranked these builders on five criteria that map to real-world adoption, not benchmarks. First, ease of use: can a non-developer ship something useful. Second, multi-agent support: can several agents split roles and hand off work. Third, integrations and tools: how many apps and built-in actions an agent can reach. Fourth, pricing clarity, including whether the free tier is a lasting plan or a countdown. Fifth, fit: who each tool is genuinely built for. Every free-plan figure below was re-checked against the vendor's own pricing page or documentation on September 23, 2026.


No single tool wins every category, which is why this is a ranked list and not a coronation. A solo founder automating lead research has different needs than a bank building an internal document assistant. The sections below say plainly who each builder suits, and name at least two things each one does well. For the underlying concepts, the[agent loop](https://www.taskade.com/wiki/ai-agents/agent-loop) and[multi-agent teams](https://www.taskade.com/wiki/ai-agents/multi-agent-teams) wiki entries are good companions.


### 1. Taskade: Best for No-Code Multi-Agent Teams


[Taskade](https://www.taskade.com/agents) is the best no-code AI agent builder for teams that want a group of agents working inside a shared workspace, with a free plan and paid plans from $10 per month billed annually. You describe an agent in plain language, give it tools, and connect it to your projects. Where most no-code tools build one assistant, Taskade builds a team: several agents split roles and hand work to each other, backed by[persistent memory](https://www.taskade.com/wiki/ai-agents/agent-memory) so context carries across sessions.


**Free plan (verified Sep 2026):** 1 agent with 1 knowledge item, 3 Genesis apps, 10 automation runs a month, and 6,000 one-time credits to start. That agent still publishes to a public, shareable link on Free — publishing is gated by role, not plan — so the real limit is depth per agent, not whether you can ship one.


Two genuine strengths stand out. First, breadth in one place: agents, a workspace database, 100+ bidirectional[integrations](https://www.taskade.com/integrations) , and[automations](https://www.taskade.com/automate) live together, so an agent can research, write to a project, and trigger a workflow without leaving the app. Second, model choice: 15+ frontier models from OpenAI, Anthropic, and open-weight providers, plus a large built-in toolset including web search, code execution, file analysis, and custom slash commands. Role-based access runs from Owner to Viewer.


The honest tradeoff: Taskade is not a code framework, so engineers who want low-level control over agent graphs may prefer CrewAI, and Free's 1-agent ceiling means a real multi-agent team needs a paid plan. If your team wants to ship a public agent without managing infrastructure, it is the most complete no-code option on a plan that never expires.[Start building free](https://www.taskade.com/create) or browse real builds in the[community gallery](https://www.taskade.com/apps) .


### 2. Gumloop: Best for Visual Data Workflows, Now a Trial


[Gumloop](https://www.gumloop.com/) is the strongest no-code builder for visual, data-heavy automation, with a drag-and-drop canvas where each node is a step. It grew popular for scraping, enrichment, and document processing, the kind of work where you want to see the whole pipeline laid out as connected boxes. Pro pricing sits around $37 per month with a large monthly credit allotment and unlimited seats, and Enterprise is custom.


**Free plan (verified Sep 2026):** there is not one anymore. Gumloop removed its permanent, credit-based free plan around July 30, 2026. New signups now get a 14-day free trial of the full Pro plan, offered only on monthly billing — choosing annual billing skips the trial and goes straight to a paid signup. If you are comparing this guide against an older Gumloop write-up that quotes a lasting $0 tier, that plan no longer exists.


Gumloop does two things especially well. Its canvas is genuinely approachable for non-developers moving structured data between apps, and its library of prebuilt nodes covers common web and AI steps so you rarely start from a blank page. It is a favorite for marketing and operations teams that live in spreadsheets and want AI in the loop without code.


The tradeoff is scope, and now duration. Gumloop is workflow-first rather than agent-team-first, so it shines for repeatable pipelines more than for open-ended multi-agent reasoning, and credit costs can climb as flows get busy. With the free plan gone, you now have 14 days on monthly billing to decide before the trial ends — plan your evaluation accordingly.


### 3. Lindy: Best for AI-Native Personal Assistants


[Lindy](https://www.lindy.ai/) is the best builder for AI-native personal assistants that handle email, calendars, and meetings, with a polished interface and a large template library. You create "Lindies" that trigger on events, such as a new email or a booked call, and take action on your behalf. Lindy has no permanent free tier, and its own pricing page lists plans starting around $29.99 per user a month, with individual tiers commonly running $49.99 and up depending on usage.


**Free plan (verified Sep 2026):** a 7-day trial, full stop — there is no $0 plan to fall back to once it ends. Budget your evaluation to that window.


Two strengths make Lindy stand out. Its onboarding and templates are among the smoothest in the category, so first-time users get a working assistant quickly. And its focus on inbox, scheduling, and meeting automations is deep, which is exactly what many solo professionals and small teams want first.


The tradeoffs are cost and openness. Lindy meters every action in credits, so heavy workflows add up, and there is no permanent free plan for long-term testing. It is a closed ecosystem, so you trade some flexibility for a refined out-of-the-box experience. For assistants that must live inside a broader team workspace, a platform-first tool fits better.


### 4. n8n: Best for Self-Hosting and Developer Control


[n8n](https://n8n.io/) is the best agent builder for teams that want to self-host and keep full control of their data, and it is free and unlimited when you run the open-source Community Edition yourself. Its node-based editor now includes AI agent steps, so you can blend deterministic workflow logic with agent reasoning in one canvas. Cloud plans start near $24 per month for a set number of executions, while self-hosting costs only your own server.


**Free plan (verified Sep 2026):** n8n Cloud gives you a 14-day trial, not a lasting free tier. Self-hosting the Community Edition is free and unlimited indefinitely, under the Sustainable Use License, as long as you run and maintain your own server.


n8n earns its place two ways. It has one of the largest integration libraries in the space, with hundreds of app nodes, and it charges per workflow execution rather than per step, which keeps pricing fair as flows grow complex. The AI agent nodes are free at the platform level, so you only pay your own model provider for tokens.


The tradeoff is that n8n leans toward technical users. Self-hosting means you own the ops, and complex logic can feel closer to low-code than pure no-code. For engineers or ops teams comfortable with that, it is a powerful, portable choice. See our[tool use history](https://www.taskade.com/blog/tool-use-history) for how agents learned to call tools like these in the first place.


### 5. Relay.app: Shut Down in 2026 — Here's Where Its Users Went


[Relay.app](https://www.relay.app/) is no longer a live option, so skip straight past it if you see it recommended elsewhere. It used to be a strong pick for human-in-the-loop approvals, blending AI steps, human confirmation, and visual logic so an agent could draft a reply or classify a ticket and pause for a person to sign off before sending — a free plan with 200 automated steps plus 500 AI credits a month, and a Professional plan at $19 a month billed annually, made it a common "best free" entry through mid-2026.


**What happened:** Relay.app told customers on July 16, 2026 that it was shutting down, without giving a reason. Free accounts and all their data were permanently deleted on August 15, 2026 at 23:59 PT. Paid subscriptions were cancelled immediately with prorated refunds, and paying customers kept access through September 14, 2026 at 23:59 PT to export their data before the shutdown became final. New signups and free-to-paid upgrades were turned off well before that date.


**Where to go instead:** if human-in-the-loop approval was the draw,[Zapier Agents](https://zapier.com/agents) and[n8n](https://n8n.io/) both support an approval step inside a larger workflow on their free tiers, and[Make](https://www.make.com/) covers the same no-code, workflow-first ground with 1,000 free operations a month. None of the three is a drop-in clone, so budget time to rebuild your Relay.app flows rather than expecting a straight import. Any 2026 "best free AI agent builder" list that still recommends Relay.app has not been rechecked since July.


### 6. Zapier Agents: Best for Extending a Zapier Stack


[Zapier Agents](https://zapier.com/agents) is the best pick if your team already lives in Zapier, because it adds AI agents on top of an ecosystem of thousands of connected apps. The free tier includes 400 activities per month, and a Pro tier runs about $33.33 per month billed annually for 1,500 activities ($50/month on monthly billing). Agents draw on a separate activity quota rather than the task quota Zapier uses for its classic Zaps.


**Free plan (verified Sep 2026):** 400 activities a month, forever, with a single agent run capped at 10 activities on Free (40 on paid plans) — an activity is any billable step, so a trigger firing, a knowledge lookup, and an action all count. That is real integration work, not a demo mode. What Free does not do is publish an agent publicly: Zapier Agents only lets you share a clone-able template link, so anyone who opens it gets their own copy under their own account. An embeddable, public-facing chat widget needs Zapier's separate Chatbots product, which has its own free plan for up to 2 chatbots.


The strengths are reach and familiarity. Zapier connects to more apps than almost anyone, so an agent can act across your existing stack immediately, and there is nothing new to learn if your workflows already run there. The free activities make it easy to try before committing.


The tradeoffs are cost layering and depth. Agents are a separately metered add-on, so heavy use stacks on top of your Zapier bill, and the agent capabilities are newer and shallower than in agent-first platforms. For teams whose center of gravity is already Zapier, though, it is the path of least resistance.


### 7. StackAI: Best for Regulated Enterprises


[StackAI](https://www.stackai.com/) is the best no-code agent builder for regulated, compliance-heavy organizations, offering SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA, and on-premise deployment. Its free tier includes 500 workflow runs per month with a starter credit allowance, and production usage is handled through custom Enterprise pricing. StackAI is built for internal tools like document assistants and retrieval workflows where data handling rules are strict.


**Free plan (verified Sep 2026):** 500 runs a month across 2 projects, forever-free, with real actions available through REST and Slack. There is no self-serve paid tier to graduate to — production usage moves straight to custom Enterprise pricing, so the free tier is where most small teams will stay.


Two strengths define it. Its compliance posture is genuinely enterprise-grade, which is decisive for healthcare, finance, and legal teams, and its retrieval and document-grounding features suit knowledge-heavy internal apps. Private model deployment and audit logging come with the Enterprise tier.


The tradeoff is fit and transparency. Enterprise pricing is custom and opaque, and the platform is overkill for individuals or small teams who do not need certifications. If you are building compliant internal tools at a larger company, StackAI is squarely aimed at you. For the grounding techniques it relies on, see our[RAG retrieval history](https://www.taskade.com/blog/rag-retrieval-history) .


### 8. Microsoft Copilot Studio: Best for Microsoft 365 Shops


[Microsoft Copilot Studio](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot/microsoft-copilot-studio) is the best agent builder for organizations standardized on Microsoft 365, with deep ties to Teams, SharePoint, and Dataverse. Pricing is consumption-based in Copilot Credits, with message packs at $200 per month for 25,000 credits, or pay-as-you-go at roughly $0.01 per credit. Costs scale with agent complexity: a simple answer uses about one credit, while an autonomous agent action can use 25 or more.


**Free plan (verified Sep 2026):** none. Copilot Studio has no standalone $0 tier — every build draws on purchased Copilot Credits or an existing Microsoft 365 Copilot seat from the first agent you create. If a lasting free plan is a hard requirement, this is the one entry on this list that cannot meet it.


Its strengths are ecosystem and governance. If your data and identity already sit in Microsoft, Copilot Studio agents plug in with minimal friction, and administration flows through the Power Platform admin center your IT team already knows. It supports autonomous agents that trigger on events.


The tradeoffs are forecasting and lock-in. Consumption pricing is hard to predict, so teams must estimate credit use carefully, and the value is concentrated inside the Microsoft stack. For a Microsoft-first enterprise, that is exactly the point; for anyone else, it adds complexity.


### 9. CrewAI: Best for Developers Building Agent Crews


[CrewAI](https://www.crewai.com/) is the best framework for developers who want to build multi-agent crews in code, and its open-source core is free under an MIT license. You define agents with roles, goals, and tools in Python, then orchestrate them as a crew that collaborates on a task. A managed cloud, CrewAI AMP, adds a hosted runtime with a free tier of limited executions, paid plans from around $25 per month, and custom Enterprise pricing.


**Free plan (verified Sep 2026):** two separate free paths, and both last indefinitely. The open-source framework is free and unlimited on your own infrastructure under the MIT license — you only pay your model provider. CrewAI Studio, the managed cloud, adds a forever-free tier capped at 50 executions a month and 1 crew before you need AMP's paid plans.


CrewAI's strengths are control and adoption. It gives engineers precise control over how agents coordinate, and it has become one of the most widely used open-source agent frameworks, with tens of millions of downloads and a large community. You can run it entirely on your own stack with no license cost.


The tradeoff is obvious: CrewAI requires Python and DevOps, so it is not for non-developers, and you own hosting, monitoring, and scaling. For engineering teams building custom agent pipelines, that control is the draw. Our[AI agents history](https://www.taskade.com/blog/ai-agents-history) traces how frameworks like this emerged.


### 10. OpenAI AgentKit: Best for OpenAI-Native Prototypes


[OpenAI AgentKit](https://openai.com/index/introducing-agentkit/) launched at DevDay in October 2025 as a toolkit for building agents in the OpenAI ecosystem, including a visual Agent Builder, an embeddable ChatKit UI, an Evals testing framework, and a Connector Registry. There is no separate platform fee: you pay standard API token pricing for the models and tools your agent calls, which makes it cheap to prototype until a workflow actually runs.


**Free plan (verified Sep 2026):** there was never a subscription to begin with, only token pricing — and now there is an expiration date on top of it. Do not start a new build on the visual Agent Builder; treat this entry as historical.


Its strengths are integration and cost model. For teams already building on OpenAI models, AgentKit keeps everything in one place, and the pay-per-token model means no subscription before you ship. The visual canvas made early prototyping fast.


The critical caveat: OpenAI has announced it is winding down the visual Agent Builder and Evals, becoming read-only on October 31, 2026 and shutting down on November 30, 2026, and points builders to its Agents SDK and ChatGPT workspace agents instead. ChatKit remains available. If you want a no-code builder you can rely on for the long term, one of the stable platforms above is a safer bet. For the plumbing underneath, see our[MCP protocol history](https://www.taskade.com/blog/mcp-protocol-history) .

## No-Code Builders vs Developer Frameworks


No-code builders and developer frameworks solve the same problem from opposite ends, and the right choice depends on whether you have engineers to spare. No-code tools like Taskade, Gumloop, and Lindy trade some control for speed, so a non-developer can ship an agent the same day. Frameworks like CrewAI trade speed for control, giving engineers precise command over agent coordination at the cost of setup, hosting, and maintenance.

## Common Mistakes When Choosing an Agent Builder


The most common mistake is picking a builder by demo instead of by fit. A tool that looks great in a two-minute video can still be the wrong shape for your team, your data, or your budget. The table below lists the traps we see most and what to do instead.


Mistake Do instead


Choosing by demo, not by fit Match the builder to who uses it and where your data lives


Ignoring how usage is metered Compare credit or execution models before you scale


Building one big agent for everything Split work across a team of focused agents


Skipping human review on risky steps Add approvals for anything customer-facing


No plan for memory or state Confirm the tool keeps context across sessions


That third row matters more than it looks. Splitting a hard job across several focused agents, each with a clear role, tends to beat one agent trying to do everything. That is the pattern behind[multi-agent teams](https://www.taskade.com/wiki/ai-agents/multi-agent-teams) , and it is why we covered[agentic design patterns](https://www.taskade.com/blog/agentic-design-patterns) separately. Good[context engineering](https://www.taskade.com/wiki/ai/context-engineering) and clear[agent permissions](https://www.taskade.com/wiki/ai-agents/agent-permissions) prevent most of the failures Gartner warns about.
